answer: Like a jetty that only lets boats dock after they have paid for a berth, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can transact. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes, and misbehavior burns the deposit. Meanwhile honest agents drift in on a zephyr of low fees: one stake, earned back through good work, opens the whole meadow of markets. The cost scales with the attack, not with the defense.
